says: Native Droid plugin layouts use a `.factory-plugin/` directory.
Droid does not require or read the fields inside `plugin.json`. It identifies an installed plugin from its marketplace entry name and registered marketplace name.
Plugin hooks live at `hooks/hooks.json` and may reference scripts in the plugin
Droid expands `${DROID_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, `$DROID_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, and `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` to the installed plugin cache path when the plugin loads.
`marketplace add` takes a marketplace, not a plugin, so a plugin directory on its own is rejected
droid plugin marketplace add ./my-marketplace / droid plugin install my-plugin@my-marketplace --scope user
`plugins[].source` | Yes | Relative path string or source object.
Absolute paths and paths that escape the marketplace directory are rejected.
`name` | Yes | Manifest metadata. The registered name is derived from the source or set by the `extraKnownMarketplaces` key.
Exit code 2 | Blocking or corrective feedback. PreToolUse blocks the tool call
Any other non-zero exit | Non-blocking error. Droid records stderr and continues where the event permits.
deny | Blocks the tool call and sends the reason to Droid.
ask | Forces a user confirmation prompt.
allowManagedHooksOnly | When true, only org-managed hooks and hooks from org-enabled plugins load.

silent_on: How a local path's registered marketplace name is derived: chock's default marketplace folder is named `chock-local`, the name its marketplace.json carries, so either derivation gives the same name. A plugin manifest field Droid reads: it reads none, so chock writes name, version and description as source metadata.
disagrees: The hooks page says `ask` forces a confirmation prompt; agentseam's vendor data (verdicts.degrade_notes.escalate) says Droid's ask does not force one and degrades it to a block. chock labels from agentseam's data and reports the disagreement.
